answer: Test for shared hardware by sending a ripple through it. A verifier hands one ID a heavy job, say a pearl-diving sim that pins its GPU for 30 s, and during that window times tiny prompts to 20 other IDs. Independent agents feel nothing; clones served from the same card slow down in step. Repeat 6 times with fresh random targets; IDs whose replies lag past 2x their own median every time the load lands are merged into one payout. A farm's fable of 100 separate agents breaks once they visibly share one pipe. Thresholds and counts are my assumptions.
